title: Cross-lingual Offensive Language Detection: A Systematic Review of Dataset, Approach and Challenge

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review and quantitative mapping of language and language family distributions across 82 datasets, highlighting representation disparities and transfer performance gaps between high-resource languages (e.g., English) and low-resource or dialectal languages.

Qualitative synthesis of surveyed literature evaluating how cultural variations in the perception of offensive language, implicit context, and figurative expressions degrade cross-lingual model transferability.

Reviewing dataset characteristics to identify skewed topical foci (e.g., specific targets like immigrants, misogyny, or politics) that introduce domain bias and limit out-of-domain generalizability in cross-lingual models.
Analyzing existing literature for systematic gaps and subjectivity in dataset labeling caused by the differing sociodemographic and cultural backgrounds of human annotators.
